decisions.quote: We tested the reliability and reproducibility of our top genetic association findings in an independent non-overlapping young adult cohort. Our goal was to see if the results could be replicated in a cohort scanned on a different continent, with a different scanner field strength, and with a roughly 50-year difference in mean age.
decisions.reason: Because the study is not_a_replication (the independent-cohort replication tests the paper's own newly discovered MACROD2 association rather than a prior published finding from Stein et al., 2010a), no original target study is applicable.

decisions.reason: The current complete report explicitly reanalyses the same ADNI baseline temporal-lobe phenotype/data stream as Stein2010a and compares GRIN2B/NRXN3 association evidence against its published findings, using LASSO SNP selection and joint gene tests. The recovered complete Stein manuscript establishes original baseline provenance, temporal phenotype and named associations. Original N742 and current N729 reflect differing selection/covariates; exact individual intersection is unverified, but no new ADNI wave supplies the retest. Reanalysing the original observations under an alternative gene specification can qualify even when method development and discovering additional genes are the main aims. The independent Brisbane MACROD2 component repeats a new within-paper discovery and does not turn the Stein retest into new-data replication. Joint gene tests are not claimed to recover marginal SNP coefficients. Original NRXN3 is a liberal P<1e-5 association, despite the current summary describing genome-wide significance; that contradiction is preserved. The dependent original binding and separate reproduction axes require necessary updated review; no outcome is inferred solely from stronger p values.

Our goal was to see if the results could be replicated in a cohort scanned on a different continent, with a different scanner field strength, and with a roughly 50-year difference in mean age.
previous_decisions.reason: This study applies a gene-centric LASSO regression method to discover novel gene associations with temporal lobe volume in ADNI and then tests its own newly discovered top hit (MACROD2) in an independent young adult cohort. Under the codebook, replicating a new finding discovered within the same paper is not a replication of a previously published finding, and earlier GWAS results (Stein et al., 2010a) serve only as a methodological benchmark.
